title: Starship Flight 15: the first attempt to catch both stages
seoTitle: Starship Flight 15: launch time, countdown and what to watch
description: Starship Flight 15 targets Friday 13 November 2026 from Starbase Pad 2: live countdown, the double-catch plan, why the heat shield matters, and where to watch.
ogImageAlt: Starship Flight 15 title card on a dark background with the Supercharged Daily bolt
summary: SpaceX is targeting Starship Flight 15 for Friday 13 November 2026 from Pad 2 at Starbase, pending regulatory approval. The 75-minute window opens at 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC). That is a published window, not a guaranteed lift-off time.

For the first time SpaceX plans to try to catch both stages with the tower: Super Heavy minutes after launch, and the Ship after a flight of more than 22 hours. SpaceX's flight plan has the Ship deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and make roughly 14 orbits before its deorbit burn; reports put the orbit at about 275 km.

If both catches work, it would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system. The tower has caught a Super Heavy booster three times, on Flights 5, 7 and 8 (October 2024 to March 2025); it has never caught a Ship.

heatShield.lead: Bringing the Ship home intact means surviving re-entry, and that is the heat shield's job.

points.text: Thousands of small hexagonal tiles cover the Ship's windward side. Because the Ship is mostly a plain cylinder, most tiles can share one shape and the rest are machined to fit, CNBC reported in August 2021.
In a 2019 test SpaceX heated tiles to about 1,650 K (around 1,377 °C or 2,510 °F), its estimate of orbital re-entry temperature, Digital Trends reported.
Most tiles are attached mechanically rather than glued, and SpaceX makes them in-house, according to Air & Space (December 2021). The space shuttle's glued tiles needed long repairs between flights.

updates.text: SpaceX lists Flight 15 as soon as Friday 13 November, 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC), 75-minute window, pending regulatory approval.

We checked this page against sources. The heat shield has thousands of tiles (CNBC), not a confirmed 18,000; the temperature is SpaceX's 2019 test figure (about 1,377 °C), not 1,400 °C; two unsourced claims (the gap-sealing felt and the tile factory's output) were removed; the booster-catch count (three) and the 14 orbits are now attributed.
